channel.title: Papers on Raman Ebrahimi
channel.description: Recent content in Papers on Raman Ebrahimi

item.title: Strategic Classification Has a Missing Lever: Audit Risk
item.description: Strategic classification with a second lever: alongside the classifier, the decision maker designs which features get audited and how hard, which changes what is worth gaming.

item.title: Strategic Opinion Manipulation in Multiplex Networks
item.description: When a platform merges opinions reported across several networks, agents can report differently on each; the resulting equilibrium distorts consensus and overstates polarization.

item.title: Visibility Design and Strategic Reasoning
item.description: Dashboards, feeds and leaderboards decide whom agents think they are playing against; this paper treats that visibility as a design lever and derives how it shapes aggregate behavior.

item.title: The Architecture of Illusion: Network Opacity and Strategic Escalation
item.description: The Connected Minds model: agents reason iteratively but observe a sample biased by their network position, so opacity makes them overestimate others and escalate.

item.title: Layers of a City: Network-Based Insights into San Diego's Transportation Ecosystem
item.description: A network view of San Diego's transportation system, layer by layer, and what its structure says about access and resilience.

item.title: Extended Horizons: Multi-hop Awareness in Network Games
item.description: This paper proposes K-hop network (security) games, in which agents have extended awareness of network effects.

item.title: Multiplex and Multilayer Network Games
item.description: This paper proposes new models of multiplex network games to capture the different modalities of interactions among strategic agents, and multilayer network games to capture their interactions over multiple action dimensions.

item.title: Semantic Navigation in Information Networks: A Case Study of the WikiRace
item.description: This paper presents a systematic evaluation of navigation strategies for the WikiRace task.

item.title: Strategic Classification with Behavioral Agents
item.description: This paper proposes a strategic classification model that considers behavioral biases in human responses to algorithms.
